text:
leah: quick idea — thinking about simplifying the streaming scheduler topology to avoid global locks. sketch: per-worker micro-queues + a tiny shared draining coordinator that runs DRR for fairness. want feedback before I spin an RFC.

omar: +1 on local queues to reduce contention. main worry is starvation when requests are lots of short ones interleaved with long ones. how do we prevent a noisy short-req tenant from starving others? :thinking:

leah: plan is soft admission: a small fastpath queue for short requests (low latency), and a main queue for everything else. fastpath has strict size cap; if it overflows we demote to main. demotion is rate-limited. idea is local -> global fallback rather than global enqueue always.

kevin: sounds promising. metric-wise we'll need per-queue p50/p99, queue_len, and a global DRR credit gauge. otherwise it becomes hard to tie back regressions to the topology change.

maya: one more constraint — streaming/grpc sessions leak large KV caches if we bounce them between workers. we probably need session affinity hashing for streams so we keep cache locality. for non-streaming unary calls we can be looser.

leah: agreed. proposal: session-affinity by session_id_hash for streaming. fallback to rr for stateless or when a worker is overloaded. rough config sketch:
```
queue:
  topology: per-worker
  fastpath_size: 8
  demote_threshold_ms: 12
  demote_rate_limit_per_worker: 2/s
  affinity: session_hash
```

omar: micro-question — how to validate headroom oscillation won't make things worse? we should simulate with a mix of short bursts and sustained large requests, measure p99 tokens and fraction of demotions. recommend local sim + canary shard.

kevin: for rollout safety add a canary toggle that keeps old global queueing for X% of traffic. also a guard: max_demotions_per_sec and queue_len thresholds that flip to global for affected worker if tripped.

sre-bot: alert stub: queued_overflow_alert when worker_queue_len > 200 for 10s. autopage policy: page on sustained p99 increase > 30% for 5m.

leah: thanks all. i'll draft a short RFC with simulation results, rollout gates, and telemetry to add (per-queue gauges + demotion counters). assigning @kevin and @maya to help with perf harness and affinity tests. i'll open the RFC tomorrow. :+1:
